ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and clients against: (i) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) OFAC SDN List; (iii) the Canadian consolidated sanctions list maintained by Global Affairs Canada under SEMA; (iv) the Criminal Code terrorism financing and FACE foreign-corruption listings; and (v) FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) determinations covering foreign and domestic PEPs, family members, and close associates. Purpose-built corporate services providers and BC counsel acting as reporting entities must perform risk-based client due diligence, enhanced due diligence for high-risk jurisdictions, and ongoing transaction monitoring for PCT fee wires to official patent offices.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.banking_aml_risk_tier_override: Low_Risk_Standard based on ISIC 7490 patent prosecution agency scope; heightened CDD applies when UBO resides in a FATF-high-risk or monitored jurisdiction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Corporate Registry - Corporate Online (https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Business Corporations Act (SBC 2002, c. 57) and the BC Name Rules, corporate names must be in English or French (or a transliteration into the Latin alphabet) and must include a mandatory legal element (e.g., Limited, Incorporated, Corporation, Inc., Ltd., Corp., or French equivalents). Names appearing in non-Latin scripts require an approved transliteration. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing BC corporate name, registered trademark, or reserved name; the Corporate Online system runs a provincial name search and, where applicable, a NUANS-style report.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trust Company, Insurance, Assurance, Broker
Medical, Barrister, Solicitor, Lawyer, Attorney, Notary
British Columbia (in a Crown or public-authority connotation)
Patent and Trademark Office (implying an official government registry)
PCT, WIPO, International (implying official international institution status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the name request is cancelled and the applicant may (1) file a written reconsideration request with the BC Registrar of Companies within 30 days, citing the applicable Name Rule and providing legal argument; (2) submit a new name request through Corporate Online (fee CAD 30) with an amended name; or (3) where the refusal relates to a sensitive token, obtain prior written consent or approval from the relevant regulator (e.g., CPA Canada for an accounting connotation, BC Securities Commission for a broker term, CPATA for patent registry terms) before re-filing. If the Registrar maintains a final statutory refusal, judicial review may be available in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Business Corporations Act; legal counsel should be engaged for that remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. British Columbia requires a registered and records office located at a physical street address within BC where service of process may be accepted; a mail-only virtual address fails the statutory physical-address test. A registered-agent service that maintains a physical BC address and accepts process is acceptable for a standard business corporation. For a regulated patent prosecution agency, CPATA requires a bona fide place of business and competent professional oversight; a purely virtual office with no local records or responsible agent is discouraged and will attract enhanced corporate-substance review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated under 5% annual likelihood of unannounced physical inspection by the BC Corporate Registry for a low-risk knowledge-based professional corporation; moderate risk of 10-25% for Canada Revenue Agency corporate substance and residency reviews in the first three years; elevated risk above 30% if the UBO transparency register is incomplete, the registered office is purely virtual, or treaty-benefit claims are made without local substantive activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, ss. 13-30 (incorporation); s. 32 (articles); s. 128 (share capital); s. 173 (registered office); s. 173.1 (records).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registry Services, Corporate and Business Registries, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles (Form 1/Form 1A) filed electronically via Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; one or more shares may be issued without initial payment. No escrow or capital contribution is required. Authorized capital is determined by the articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation be incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) with registered office at 1055 West Georgia Street, Vancouver, BC V6E 3P3, Canada; RESOLVED that the authorized share capital be 100,000 common shares without par value, of which 10,000 common shares are hereby allotted and issued to the sole shareholder for CAD 100 lawful consideration; RESOLVED that the Pre-Incorporation Agreement be adopted and any subscriptions ratified; RESOLVED that the President and Secretary-Treasurer be appointed; RESOLVED that banking resolutions be approved; and RESOLVED that the directors execute all filings and engagements necessary to commence patent and trademark prosecution services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry via BC Name Request Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Request online using a NUANS-style search to verify availability and obtain a Name Reservation or Name Approval. Choose a distinctive corporate name ending in “Corp.” or “Inc.”, or use a numbered company if no name is selected.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged, file a revised Name Request within 14 days; further clarification may be submitted to the Corporate Registry by written submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles, authenticated by the applicant; select the company’s registered office and first directors and set the share structure. Payment of the filing fee is made online and electronic certification is issued upon approval.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director (each director)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for defect, correct the identified particulars and resubmit electronically; any filing fee is credited toward the corrected filing within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, prepare and maintain the articles, organizational records, share register, and directors’ register. Hold the first board meeting and adopt the first board resolution covering allotment of shares, appointment of officers, adoption of pre-incorporation contracts, and banking authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If records are deficient, the directors may ratify omissions by a subsequent board resolution; administrative late filings are cured under s. 372 by paying a reinstatement fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax Registration and Provincial Extras
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Government of BC, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the Business Number through CRA and, if applicable, GST/HST, payroll, and income tax accounts. Also register with BC Corporate and Business Registries for provincial program accounts such as WorksafeBC and municipal business licensing through the City of Vancouver.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, obtain a letter of confirmation from BC Registry and follow CRA objecting procedure; duplicate and incomplete filings can be amended directly through CRA’s Business Registration Online portal.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA-ARC); principal portals: Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/services-businesses/business-registration-online.html) and My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html). BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) is administered by the British Columbia Ministry of Finance (https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/sales-taxes/pst).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a BC incorporated or extra-provincially registered business corporation: (1) obtain a 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online or Form RC1; (2) open program accounts: GST/HST (RT), Import/Export (RM), and Payroll (RP) if applicable; (3) online BN issuance is immediate, and the BN is the statutory TIN for all federal tax accounts; (4) register with the BC Corporate Registry for corporate legal status and with the BC Ministry of Finance for PST if taxable BC supplies are made; (5) the Canadian-resident corporation must file an annual T2 corporate income tax return; non-resident shareholders are not required to file T2 solely by virtue of ownership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Canadian-resident BC Business Corporation is taxed under Part I of the Income Tax Act on worldwide income; no pass-through or check-the-box eligibility; no territorial exemption; no tax-exempt zone status; foreign tax credits mitigate double taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box election or hybrid-mismatch election exists for Canadian incorporated entities; hybrid-mismatch rules (ITA ss. 17.1-17.7) apply automatically. Available elections: (i) ITA s. 85(1) tax-deferred rollover election for qualifying property/IP transfers; (ii) Excise Tax Act s. 156 election for closely related corporations to value intercorporate supplies at nil for GST; (iii) ITA s. 83(2) capital dividend account election; (iv) treaty-based Part XIII withholding relief for non-resident shareholders (investor-level, not entity-level).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting as monetary authority and fiscal agent for the Minister of Finance; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act; foreign exchange administration is governed by the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) and the Exchange Fund Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. E-13), with operational FX intervention executed by the Bank of Canada; no separate central-planning exchange-control administration exists in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. The Canadian dollar is freely floating with no residual exchange-control legislation. Profit remittance is unrestricted, but non-resident dividends, management fees, royalties, and interest paid by a British Columbia corporation are subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) at 25% statutory, treaty-reduced as applicable (e.g., 15% dividends and 10% royalties under the Canada-China DTA). Repatriation of capital, repayment of shareholder loans, and liquidation proceeds may be transmitted without prior regulatory approval; the only frictions are standard FINTRAC anti-money-laundering reporting (large cash transactions over CAD 10,000, cross-border EFT reporting over CAD 10,000) and income-tax arm's-length/section 15 benefit rules where advances to shareholders are involved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation on export receipts or any foreign-denominated revenue. A British Columbia corporation may lawfully maintain USD, EUR, GBP, and CNY bank accounts in Canada or abroad and may convert export or service proceeds at its treasury's discretion. FINTRAC record-keeping and reporting obligations do not restrict conversion freedom.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High as a supplementary payment rail, Low as a primary banking solution. Wise (TransferWise Canada Limited) and Payoneer are registered Money Service Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, not banks under the Bank Act; they cannot legally accept deposits or originate Canadian-dollar debits through Payments Canada rails. Their Canadian trust balances must be held at Schedule I chartered banks. The patent prosecution agency may use Wise for low-value international disbursements to foreign patent offices and associates, but the principal operating and client trust accounts must be maintained at a Canadian chartered bank to satisfy College of Patent Agents and Traders (CPAT) trust-account rules and Canadian counterparty expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian Schedule I banks require in-person or scheduled video-call identity verification for at least one signing officer. Where all directors are non-resident, remote onboarding is available through bank international desks (e.g., RBC International Business Centre) and typically requires a notarized Certificate of Incumbency, two recent utility bills, certified passport copies of each signatory, and a Canadian registered-office address (a BC registered agent's office may suffice). The BC Business Corporations Act does not mandate Canadian residence for directors; banks, however, may require a physical in-branch interview if the ultimate beneficial owner is a politically exposed person or if the entity presents low substance. A Canadian business address is strongly preferred but not statutorily mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or offshore beneficial ownership with no Canadian tax nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized updated Central Securities Register under s.114 BC Business Corporations Act; beneficial-ownership schedule naming every UBO per FINTRAC definitions; directors' resolution attesting value creation occurs in British Columbia; notarized source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, gift or sale agreements); professional reference letters from a licensed Canadian accountant and law firm; CRA Business Number confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical substance in British Columbia (mailbox-company flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC registered-office address; executed 12-month virtual-office lease with an identified Canadian provider; Canadian telephone line; CPAT patent-agent licence or pending registration with the College of Patent Agents and Traders; valid BC registry number under the BC Business Corporations Act; CRA GST/HST account confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through trust transactions (client-deposited fees routed to foreign patent offices)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated client trust account compliant with CPAT trust rules; itemized trust journal with client ledger per patent matter; signed engagement letters for each client; official fee schedules of WIPO, CIPO, USPTO, and EPO; PCT filing receipts and docket confirmations; quarterly trust reconciliation signed by an external accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments from third parties or corporate-group affiliates not disclosed as clients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed third-party payment authorization and corporate resolution by the payer; treasury attestation identifying the ultimate beneficiary of the patent services; invoice and fee-disclosure record matching payer accounting entries; enhanced due diligence file containing the payer's registry-certified beneficial-ownership certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious jurisdictions or designated-list counterparties (sanctions exposure)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time screening against OSFI consolidated sanctions lists, UN Security Council resolutions, and the Canadian Special Economic Measures Act; KYC/CDD file for every foreign associate; certification of no US OFAC nexus; compliance assurance letter from each foreign associate; legal opinion obtained under the Special Economic Measures Act where any listed counterparty appears.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share-subscription proceeds are routed via SWIFT MT103 annotated 'Share Subscription - BCBCA s.190 - CRA Business Number [xxxx]' to the bank operating account in CAD; the initiating corporate treasury must attach the executed directors' resolution authorizing the issuance, the share-subscription agreement, and a funds-verification statement. No prior approval is required under the Investment Canada Act for a de novo incorporation of a patent prosecution agency where enterprise value remains below the WTO threshold (CAD 1.298 billion for 2025 direct acquisitions). The receiving Schedule I bank files FINTRAC cross-border EFT reports within five business days for wires over CAD 10,000. Additional CAD liquidity may be injected as shareholder loans evidenced by a written promissory note carrying prescribed interest under Income Tax Act s.80.4 to avoid a deemed shareholder benefit; the corporate accountant must update the BC issued-share register and issue share certificates.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wire transfers and Payments Canada's Real-Time Rail, Large Value Transfer System, or Automated Clearing Settlement System for domestic CAD payments. Core outbound disbursements for a patent prosecution agency are: (i) WIPO international filing and designation fees in CHF, USD, or EUR via SWIFT MT103 to WIPO's Geneva account or through the WIPO e-Payment gateway; (ii) CIPO examination, maintenance, and annuity fees through the CIPO online payment interface in CAD; (iii) USPTO filing and search fees via USPTO Deposit Account or Financial Manager e-payment in USD; (iv) foreign-associate disbursements in CNY, JPY, KRW, GBP, and EUR via MT103 with the patent matter reference in field 70 Remittance Information. Standby or documentary letters of credit are permissible but uneconomic for professional-services trade; the recommended instrument is the SWIFT MT101/MT103 documentary payment instruction governed by the UCP/URC frameworks. Every outbound disbursement exceeding CAD 10,000 triggers FINTRAC cross-border EFT record-keeping and reporting and must reference a trust-account patent matter code.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards in CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP with a Schedule I bank under a master FX agreement or ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, tenor typically up to 12 months

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in offshore CNY or other restricted currencies where physical delivery is impossible, requiring an ISDA 1998 FX and Currency Option Definitions addendum and a bank credit line
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) under an ISDA Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex, used only to match the maturity of a committed overseas associate account or a finance facility

European-style FX options (CAD calls / foreign-currency puts) purchased from a Schedule I bank or registered derivatives dealer, cash-secured with no leverage, to hedge a defined patent-award receivable
Plain-vanilla spot transactions executed through the bank's FX Online portal, excluded from hedge accounting but permissible for day-to-day operating conversions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Registries), British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary date of incorporation, each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 50 (approx. USD 37) applies after the due date; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution (strike-off) by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for a private BC business corporation unless the entity is a reporting issuer under securities laws, a court order or the company's articles or unanimous shareholders' agreement require an audit, or a shareholder holding at least 5% of issued shares (or a group holding at least 10%) demands an audit under sections 198(2) and 198(4) of the Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private enterprises may apply Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises, or may be voluntarily adopted; books and records must also comply with the Canadian Income Tax Act for tax purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a transparency register of significant individuals at its registered office. Annually, as part of the Annual Report filing, the directors confirm that the register is complete and accurate. Any share transfer or change in significant individuals must be recorded promptly, with the register updated within 15 days of the company becoming aware of the change. No separate annual UBO filing to the BC Registrar is required.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Exempt from statutory audit; voluntary audit typical range: USD 5,000 - USD 12,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.0% combined top rate (15.0% federal Part I general rate + 12.0% British Columbia general corporate rate); 11.0% combined small-business rate (9.0% federal + 2.0% BC) on active business income up to CA$500,000 for a qualifying Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (CCPC)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 35% refundable Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit on eligible BC expenditures up to CA$3,000,000 for CCPCs (15% non-refundable otherwise); 10% BC SR&ED refundable/non-refundable credit; accelerated Capital Cost Allowance (CCA) on Class 44 patents and Class 50 eligible digital/data assets; no patent-box regime in Canada; all IP royalties and fee income taxed at general rates once business income exceeds the CA$500,000 small-business threshold
